Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches, 7 commits ahead of develop, tree clean. Read-only investigation — do not fix anything, do not modify anything.

This is a POST-BUILD, WHOLE-FEATURE sweep — deliberately different from testing any one step. The premise: a per-step review, however thorough, is structurally blind to a pattern applied consistently but WRONGLY across every step — it passes every individual review because each step looks internally fine on its own terms. This phase exists specifically to catch that. On this project, a systematic spacing error once survived five commits and every individual score, and was only found by looking at the whole feature together afterward.

The feature is SFCC-91 — PDP colour swatches. Four commits built it: `9f46912` (a `renderVariationAttribute` slot on `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`), `ab04241`+`6631e05` (the `ZimmColourSwatch` atom, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/`, plus a fix), `b16298e` (the `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` molecule, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/`), `7139687` (wiring both into `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`), and `2d8a9a7` (a doc-only fix). Read all of these files in full before starting.

## Direction 1 — Internal: does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric for this half. Just: is the atom and the molecule internally consistent with EACH OTHER, as if one person designed both in one sitting?

- **Recipe shape** — same `parts` convention? Same registration pattern in `theme/components/index.ts`? Same choice of plain-object vs function-form `baseStyle` where the same kind of state-dependence exists? (The atom's `selected` prop and the molecule's `isPaginated` prop are both boolean, state-dependent, single-value style switches — are they handled the same way?)
- **Component structure** — same export shape, same props-type declaration style, same JSDoc density and tone, same story categorisation, same test-file organisation?
- **Token use** — every colour/spacing value routed through `var(--zimm-*)` the same way in both files? Any place one component reaches for a token the other could have reused but didn't (i.e., the same real-world value expressed as two different token references, or one as a token and the other not)?
- **The same real-world value never typed twice in two different places** — check specifically: is the 48px swatch width ever hand-typed as a literal anywhere outside its one token definition? Is the "4 swatches per page" constant (`SWATCHES_PER_PAGE`) ever duplicated as a raw `4` anywhere instead of referencing that one constant?
- **Import conventions** — relative vs `app/`-alias paths for sibling ui-kits imports: does the atom and the molecule (and the page wiring into both) follow one consistent rule, or does each file make its own independent choice? (I know from this build's own history that at least one relative-vs-alias inconsistency was flagged mid-build and judged acceptable because BOTH conventions have real precedent elsewhere in this codebase — confirm this is still true at the current, final state, and specifically check whether the choice is at least consistent WITHIN this one feature, not just independently defensible in isolation.)

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible — that's the whole point of this direction.

## Direction 2 — External: does that shared shape conform?

Only assess this once you've established what the feature's own internal pattern actually is (Direction 1).

- **Against the exemplar precedent** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/` (the four-file pattern this build was told to mirror) and commit `227171e` (the `renderHeader` slot precedent this build's own `renderVariationAttribute` slot was told to mirror). Does the built feature actually match what those exemplars established? Where you find the exemplar itself is inconsistent about something, say which variant this feature followed and whether that was the more defensible choice — don't report a divergence from an unstable exemplar as a defect in this feature.
- **Against `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, `components.md`, `css.md`, `typescript.md`, `conventions.md`** — read all five in full. Check each rule's actual text against the WHOLE feature, not just one file. A rule that holds in the atom but not the molecule (or vice versa) is exactly what this whole-feature pass exists to catch that a per-file check would miss.
- **Against Figma, end to end** — the feature has real cited Figma nodes across its build history: `40000307:13826`/`:13831`/`40002689:3839` (the atom's three states), `40001992:51881`/`40000307:13867` (the molecule's container + label + pagination layout). You do NOT have Figma tool access in this session — instead, verify the feature's OWN internal citations of these nodes are used consistently: does every place that cites a specific Figma value (48px width, the 2:3 aspect ratio, the 8px/4px gaps, the `calc(4 * var(--zimm-scale-1200))` reserved-width value) agree with every other place that cites the same underlying design fact? A recipe comment claiming one pixel value and a test asserting a different one for the same design fact would be a real, catchable inconsistency even without live Figma access.

Every finding carries **UNIFORM** (the same issue recurs elsewhere, or represents a systemic pattern) or **ONE-OFF** (isolated to one spot). At whole-feature scope, UNIFORM findings are what this phase exists to surface — do not bury them under a longer list of one-offs.

## What NOT to do

Do not re-litigate any decision already made and recorded in `plan.md §1b` (Marcel's own decisions — ignoring the other branch, the PRD-staleness ruling, the render-slot architecture, dropping Small/Rounded, shipping pagination, dropping `backgroundColor`, keeping the value type minimal). If the build honoured a recorded decision, that is not a finding, even if you'd have chosen differently.

## Report format

Findings first, UNIFORM ones first. For each: what it is, exactly where (file:line, both/all locations if it recurs), why it matters, and CONFIRMED (you verified it directly) vs PLAUSIBLE (strong signal, not fully verified) vs UNSUPPORTED. Then what you tried to falsify and couldn't. Then what you genuinely could not check and why (no Figma access, no live BM data, etc. — be specific).

    feat(product-view): add renderHeader slot for caller-supplied header content
    
    Adds one optional prop to ProductView so a caller can supply the header block, and
    corrects two documentation claims in the same file that were false or misleading.
    
    The slot
    ---------
    renderHeader?: (props: ProductViewHeaderProps) => React.ReactNode
    
    Its default renders the same private ProductViewHeader the base file renders inline, with
    the identical six values, so omitting it is behaviour-preserving. Both header call sites
    route through it — base renders the header twice behind responsive display arrays, and a
    slot only one of them honoured would be a silent half-override.
    
    Prop, default and call sites are one atomic unit, not three separable edits: deleting the
    default alone produces TS2722 at both call sites.
    
    Why the default export rather than a named-export wrapper
    ----------------------------------------------------------
    overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that
    wraps the default. That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props

## Finding 2 — ONE-OFF (recurrence risk) — `ZimmColourSwatch`'s href-less branch is an inoperable ARIA radio

**Where:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:85-96` (the `<chakra.span role="radio" tabIndex={...}>` branch rendered when `href` is absent), type at `:13-33` (`ZimmColourSwatchProps` has no select-callback prop of any kind).

**What's wrong:** when `href` is absent, the atom renders `role="radio"`, `aria-checked`, and a real `tabIndex` (0 or -1) on a plain `<span>` — but there is no `onClick`, no `onKeyDown`, and no prop anywhere in the type surface a caller could use to wire one in. The element announces to assistive tech as an operable radio and can receive keyboard focus, but nothing happens on click, Enter, or Space. I compared directly against `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/swatch.jsx` (the component this replaces): base's `Swatch` always renders as a real `<Button>` and, specifically in its own no-`href` case, wires `onClick`/`onMouseEnter` back to a `handleSelect` prop it accepts — i.e. base's equivalent really is operable without a href. The atom's own docstring explicitly names this exact scenario ("Absent for the quick-view-modal path... the swatch must not navigate") but ships no way to make it work — a future consumer would need to change this file's prop surface, not just its own caller.

**Rule/AC violated:** `components.md`'s accessibility intent + AGENTS.md's stated WCAG 2.2 AA target (a `role="radio"` control the WAI-ARIA APG requires be Space-operable, that cannot be operated by any input). It doesn't trip the literal ast-grep "onClick without role/tabIndex/onKeyDown" pattern, since there's no `onClick` at all — the gap is one level more fundamental than that rule anticipates.

**Severity:** 🟡 should-fix — nothing in production is affected today (the only current caller, `product-detail/index.tsx`, always supplies `href`; confirmed by reading its wiring), but this is a real, load-bearing gap for the exact future use the component's own comments anticipate, and unlike this codebase's other genuinely-incomplete states (e.g. `swatch-group`'s disabled-colour logic, logged in overrideStyling.md's "Known gaps"), it isn't logged anywhere. **CONFIRMED** — verified by reading both files' full source directly. **ONE-OFF** today; flagged for recurrence risk since the shape (href-optional presentational atom, no escape-hatch callback) could get copied as a template.
